title: Treat the typeface as a product system
principle: Rasmus Andersson’s Inter (rsms.me / GitHub) shows type as engineered product: metrics, optical sizes, features, and UI intent documented publicly. When choosing or generating UI type, specify the system (features, tabular nums, weights) not just a font name.
procedure: Pick a UI typeface with clear metrics for screens.
Define weight roles and size scale; enable font-feature-settings you need (tnum, ss##).
Test at small sizes; reject pretty display faces for dense UI.
Document loading strategy (subset, fallbacks) as part of design.
examplePrompts:
Specify type as a system (rsms / Inter craft mindset):
- Family + fallbacks
- Weight roles
- Size scale
- Features (tabular nums, etc.)
- Loading/subset notes
Apply to this denser settings UI; reject decorative display fonts.
Replace this marketing font in the data table with a UI face + tnum.
promptWhy: tnum/data UI is a concrete check.
tips: No endorsement of Inter as mandatory—use as craft reference.
antiPatterns: Display type in dense data UI.
